lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.era: A test before an operating system
archive_evidence.history: The variable-precision calculator later known as dc was an early B program tested on the PDP-11 before Unix was ready there.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Brian Kernighan wrote most of the explanatory text of their 1978 C book. Ritchie wrote its language reference and a chapter on the Unix interface.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: B was the immediate language predecessor of C. Unix was the operating system whose development helped shape C.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Using a higher-level language helped the team express systems logic. Later ports exposed the assumptions that had to change for new machines.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: On Unix, an editor, a compiler and a shell can each do different work. C can be used to implement those tools or the system on which they run.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Evolution of the Unix Time-sharing System
